title: Oceans, Rivers and Mountains
intro: Dive deep and climb high with questions about the shape of our planet.

questions.prompt: In which mountain range is Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest is part of the Himalayas, a mountain range in Asia that includes many of the world's highest peaks.

questions.prompt: Which ocean lies between Europe and Africa on one side and the Americas on the other?
questions.explanation: The Atlantic Ocean separates Europe and Africa from North and South America.

questions.prompt: The Amazon River flows through Brazil.
questions.explanation: The Amazon flows across South America, much of it through Brazil and its huge rainforest.

questions.prompt: On which continent is Mount Kilimanjaro?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro, in Tanzania, is the highest mountain in Africa.

questions.prompt: About what percentage of all the water on Earth is in the ocean?
questions.explanation: About 97 per cent of Earth's water is in the ocean. Most of the rest is frozen in ice or found in lakes, rivers and underground.

questions.prompt: What is the deepest known point in the ocean called?
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep, in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean, is the deepest known place in the ocean, nearly 11 kilometres down.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest ocean?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is by far the largest ocean and holds more than half of the free water on Earth.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Cairo?
questions.explanation: The River Nile flows north through Egypt and its capital, Cairo, to the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.prompt: A river's mouth is where it begins.
questions.explanation: A river begins at its source. Its mouth is where it ends, usually flowing into the sea, a lake or another river.

questions.prompt: How many named oceans are there on Earth?
questions.explanation: The five oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic. They are all joined together as one global ocean.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest ocean?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean, around the North Pole, is the smallest and shallowest of the five oceans.

questions.prompt: Which ocean surrounds Antarctica?
questions.explanation: The Southern Ocean circles all the way around Antarctica and is very cold.

questions.prompt: The sea is salty because rain and rivers wash salts out of rocks on land and carry them to the ocean.
questions.explanation: Rivers carry tiny amounts of dissolved salts into the sea. When seawater evaporates, the salt stays behind.

questions.prompt: What mainly causes the tides in the ocean?
questions.explanation: The Moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans, making the water rise and fall. The Sun's pull helps too, but less.

questions.prompt: Most coasts have how many high tides each day?
questions.explanation: Most coastal places have two high tides and two low tides roughly every day.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the city of Rome?
questions.explanation: Ancient Rome grew up beside the Tiber, and the river still flows through the middle of the city today.

questions.prompt: The Nile is about how many kilometres long?
questions.explanation: The Nile is about 6,650 kilometres long and is often called the longest river in the world.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range is often used as the dividing line between Europe and Asia?
questions.explanation: The Ural Mountains run from north to south across Russia and are usually taken as part of the border between Europe and Asia.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Paris?
questions.explanation: The Seine winds through the middle of Paris, crossed by many famous bridges.

questions.prompt: The Mississippi River is in which country?
questions.explanation: The Mississippi flows south through the middle of the United States into the Gulf of Mexico.

questions.prompt: What is a smaller river or stream that flows into a bigger river called?
questions.explanation: Tributaries join the main river and add more water to it as it flows towards the sea.

questions.prompt: What is the name for flat land where a river splits into many channels before it reaches the sea?
questions.explanation: A delta forms where a river drops the mud and sand it carries, building up new land at its mouth.

questions.prompt: Rivers flow downhill.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls water downhill, so rivers flow from high ground towards lower ground and the sea.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range runs down the west side of South America?
questions.explanation: The Andes stretch for about 7,000 kilometres along the western edge of South America.

questions.prompt: Mont Blanc is the highest peak in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc stands on the border of France and Italy and is the highest mountain in the Alps.

questions.prompt: Mount Fuji, a famous snow-capped volcano, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan and is a volcano that last erupted in 1707.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in North America?
questions.explanation: Denali, in Alaska, rises to about 6,190 metres, higher than any other peak in North America.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in Wales?
questions.explanation: Yr Wyddfa, also called Snowdon, is about 1,085 metres high and is in Eryri (Snowdonia) National Park.

questions.prompt: Which sea between Israel and Jordan is so salty that people float easily in it?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea is many times saltier than the ocean, and all that salt makes the water push swimmers up.

questions.prompt: A glacier is a fast-flowing river of liquid water high in the mountains.
questions.explanation: A glacier is a huge mass of ice that moves very slowly downhill, often only a few centimetres a day.
